result.reason: Nothing found kills it, but the core duty is still undefined. The law exists: JO 7897 (4 Apr 2026) lists Loi n° 2026-07 relative aux activités de sécurité privée, dated 27 Feb 2026. No decree, no named or staffed regulator, no transition deadline, and no rules on agent cards, training, insurance or registers were found. So the recurring filing work is not yet defined. The regulator is studying France's CNAPS, which runs its own e-services, so a state portal could absorb the filing core. Local guarding-ops tools (Kolonell, BanetteOne) could add a compliance module. Press gives only "hundreds of firms", no count. No small-firm exemption or repeal found. Timing risk is high; revisit once the decrees are out.

coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K08. Law 2023-06 (June 2023) is the framework; ARP opened Kaolack regional pole July 2025; 4 licensed wholesalers (Laborex, Duopharm, Ubipharm, Sodipharm per 2024 union source); no national serialisation or traceability mandate found.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Strongest lead. Bill 03/2026 on private security activities adopted by the National Assembly on 18 Feb 2026 to replace the 1978 law (law 78-40); creates a regulatory body to grant authorisations, supervise and sanction; covers guarding, escort, close protection and video surveillance. Promulgation and implementing decrees not confirmed. Rota/payroll software exists (BanetteOne, Kolonell) but regulator-facing compliance not seen. Cleaning and manpower agencies not checked.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Mining Code 2016-32 and decree 2017-459 (private/temporary quarry authorisations, quarterly and annual reports, royalties); new mining code under preparation (President asked for adoption by end 2025), not confirmed adopted. Local content is already K01. Nothing new beyond K01 apart from a weak quarry-operator idea.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: CENTIF 2024: 928 suspicious reports, almost all from banks; DNFBP participation is low and no DNFBP register or portal found. Beneficial ownership: Arrêté 24577 (2 Sept 2022) and DGID note require annual e-services declaration for RCCM-registered entities (not sole traders); decree 2025-1354 (27 Aug 2025) strengthens the extractive-chain RBE. Senegal was on the FATF list from Feb 2021 (status now not checked). Weak candidates.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Hotels need an agrément and an autorisation d'exploitation from the Direction de la réglementation touristique; tourist police campaigns against informal guest houses and furnished flats; tax about 1,000 FCFA per person per night (2025 guide). No fiche de police or platform-declaration rule found. Tourism tax is already K09 (rejected).

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Fish: mareyeur-exporteur card per approved processing unit (decree 2009-1226), DITP publishes a list of export-approved establishments (updated 6 Dec 2024); Dec 2025 minister said 230,072 t exported in 2024 and called for a regulatory framework. No catch-certificate or traceability mandate confirmed. Cashew and groundnut export taxes are covered under 22.

coverage.category: 31. Private higher-education institutions (EPES) licensing and compliance (country-specific, MESRI/DGES)
coverage.found: DGES communiqué of 29 July 2026: any opening, extension or relocation needs a full dossier; provisional agrément required; closure for non-compliance; about 298 EPES and roughly a third not fully compliant; legal basis law 94-82 and decree 2018-850. Candidate noted, details unverified.

coverage.category: 32. Personal-data and CCTV declarations to the CDP (country-specific, law 2008-12)
coverage.found: Companies with CCTV must declare to the CDP and get a récépissé (deliberation 2016-00238); sensitive processing (biometrics, health) needs prior authorisation; CDP issued formal notices and refused receipts in 2025; Feb 2026 parliamentary debate stressed prior CDP authorisation for private CCTV. 83 declarations in Q1 2025, so low volume. Generic compliance, weak.

coverage.category: 33. Beneficial-ownership register filings (country-specific, DGID arrêté 24577 / decree 2025-1354)
coverage.found: See 28. Annual and 15-day change filings on DGID e-services for RCCM entities; fine of 1M FCFA noted for some breaches (finance law 2025). Accountant-side task, close to generic accounting; weak.

coverage.category: 34. Mobile-money and agent networks (country-specific, BCEAO e-money rules)
coverage.found: BCEAO regional switch and interoperability, proposed 0.5% mobile-money transfer tax (Sept 2025, adoption unconfirmed). No agent-register or reporting duty found for sub-agents. Not enough evidence; unverified.

coverage.category: 35. Artisanal fishing: pirogue registration, fishing permits, mareyeur cards (country-specific, Fisheries Code 2015-18)
coverage.found: About 20,689 registered pirogues, 10,592 artisanal permits issued (about 51%, undated source); registration frozen since 2012 order, geolocation push; mareyeur card under decree 2009-1226. Fishers mostly offline and low spend; no new 2025-27 rule found. Weak.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Senegalese police-register (livre de police) regime for second-hand dealers or pawnbroker licensing found; searches returned only French law (art. 321-7 code pénal), so nothing transferable. No Senegalese mont-de-piété or pawn-lending regime found in 2 searches (pawn lending would fall under UEMOA/BCEAO credit rules, unconfirmed). Only relevant fact: the Dec 2024 announced ban on second-hand clothing (fripe) imports was officially denied by the Commerce ministry (conditional on textile industry revival, progressive); Colobane market is the hub. No 2025-2026 measure found. No recurring filing duty identified. Unchecked: Code pénal / Code de commerce text on registre des revendeurs, municipal market-fee regimes, fripe import rules in customs code.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Senegalese law or decree on licensing of dismantlers (casses) or end-of-life vehicle (VHU) management found. Sector described as entirely informal (SENDRA, founded 2020, aims to be first official dismantling centre; 90-day impound then depollution, per autorecyclingworld.com). Used-part shops cluster around gares routières ('venant' parts). Import-age decree of Oct 2025 (10 yrs cars/light vans, 15 yrs passenger transport, moped under 50cc banned; number 2025-1752 per one source, unverified) concerns whole vehicles, not parts. French customs treat used-parts exports to Senegal as banned (not a Senegalese text). No registers or reporting duty found, so nothing new beyond the technical-inspection debate noted in first pass. Unchecked: DEEC classified-establishment rules, Code de l'environnement provisions on scrap/ELV.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeper registration, hive register, honey export approval or traceability duty found for Senegal. Sector is small and NGO/donor-supported (FAO Casamance honey study, Dutch cooperation, UNPS union, APS Jan 2026 dispatch on kits and training certificates); no GI or qualification scheme for 'miel de Casamance'. Results on traceability were all other countries (Argentina SITA, Guatemala STDF). Unchecked: ASN honey standard, EU-export approval by the veterinary/DIREL services, any 2025-2026 apiculture law.

result.competitor: The claim that no SYCEBNL software exists is wrong. Compta Expert (Compta Expert Informatique with the Cercle Gestion et Développement, announced on ohada.com on 22/11/2023) has the SYCEBNL chart of accounts built in. It produces the financial statements and notes to the accounts automatically, without Excel, and handles fixed assets. It is sold as a lifetime licence with no annual fee, aimed at associations, NGOs, professional orders and project units. The vendor appears to be in Congo; whether it serves Senegal was not checked. TOMPRO and Sage are long-standing NGO and project accounting tools, but nothing found confirms they offer SYCEBNL modules. There are also Excel templates for the simplified regime, plus OHADA, BCT and Cercle training and accountancy firms offering migration services.
result.duty: Real, and it applies directly in Senegal through the OHADA Uniform Act on non-profit accounting (SYCEBNL), applicable since 1 Jan 2024. Every non-profit entity has to keep a donor register and an inventory book and produce annual financial statements plus an activity report, every year. Under Art. 24, managers who fail to do this face criminal penalties. There are two regimes: entities with subsidies, donations and bequests of 30M FCFA or less use the simplified cash-based regime (Système Minimal de Trésorerie, SMT); above that threshold the full system applies. That 30M figure comes from the OHADA Cotonou training report; a Cameroonian blog cites different thresholds. Not found: the Senegal-specific filing authority, the deadline, and actual enforcement. One secondary source (infoproff) claims associations are exempt from publishing accounts.
result.market: No current register count was found. The latest ANSD figure (2009 non-profit monograph) is 1,756 organisations: 1,254 associations and 307 NGOs. Thousands more associations are probably declared with the Interior Ministry (unverified). Most are small, fall under the cash-based SMT regime and have little ability to pay. The paying segment is likely a few hundred donor-funded NGOs and project units, plus their accountants.
result.reason: The duty is real, recurs every year and carries criminal penalties under OHADA SYCEBNL Art. 24. But the claim's main premise, that no SYCEBNL software exists, is contradicted: Compta Expert sells SYCEBNL-native accounting with automatic financial statements on a cheap lifetime licence. Excel templates and accountancy firms cover the small entities on the cash-based regime. The product is close to the out-of-scope 'generic accounting' exclusion. Most Senegalese associations are tiny and pay little, and Senegal-specific enforcement and filing rules were not found. The paying segment (donor-funded NGOs and projects) is small and already served by accountants and project tools. Distribution through accountants is possible, but pain and willingness to pay are both low.

result.competitor: Ops software for guarding firms is sold in francophone Africa: Agenz (Obvious Technologies), Simply Secu, BanetteOne (planning, main courante, invoicing, agent app), VigiCom MCI, and Kolonell custom builds. None was seen handling regulator authorisation filings or agent-card registers. No state portal was found for the new regulator; it may not exist yet (not verified).
result.duty: Loi n° 2026-07 relative aux activités de sécurité privée (27 Feb 2026, JO 7897 of 4 Apr 2026, p.724) is promulgated and replaces law 78-40 of 1978. Under the 1978 law the penalty was 2-6 months' prison and a fine of 100,000-500,000 FCFA. The new law creates a regulator that issues agréments, supervises and sanctions. Not reached: frequency of renewal, agent card, training, registers, reporting, transition period, implementing decrees, new penalties, and whether the regulator is operational.
result.market: There is no official count. Seneweb (18 Feb 2026) describes "hundreds of companies" and "thousands of agents". No register of licensed agencies was found.
result.reason: The law exists. Loi n° 2026-07 on private security activities, dated 27 Feb 2026, is listed in JO n° 7897 of 4 Apr 2026 and replaces law 78-40. It creates a regulator that grants agréments, supervises and sanctions. The recurring duties are not confirmed: I found no implementing decree, no detail on agent cards, registers, training or renewal, no transition deadline for existing agencies, and no sign the regulator is running yet. I did not open the full JO text (a 25 MB PDF). Generic guard-ops software (Agenz, Simply Secu, BanetteOne, Kolonell) covers planning and rounds, but none was seen doing regulator filings. The market is small: the press says "hundreds" of firms. There is a risk the regulator builds its own portal. Revisit once the decrees are out.

The reform is real, but the buyer pool is too small. OFOR (Law 2014-13, a public industrial and commercial body) delegates rural water to private operators under affermage contracts. These operators must be legal entities (personnes morales). Le Soleil names only five main operators: Aquatech, Seoh, Flexeau, Soges and Sder. A 2019 presentation mentions about 8 delegation perimeters covering about 2000 boreholes. That is a handful of mid-size firms, not a mass SME market. The duty is contractual, not a statutory duty on small businesses. ASUFOR committees are being phased out. I did not find the reporting rules or any OFOR platform, and I did not open forages-ruraux.sn. I found no competing product, but my searches did not cover this niche in depth.

Duty is real: Senegal's motorcycle registration drive began 6 Jan 2025 for bikes above 49 cc. It needs carte grise, plate (about 28,000 FCFA) and insurance. The minister announced systematic enforcement from end of March 2026, with about 35,000 cartes grises still to issue. I found no Senegalese app or private service for the core job; the process is counter-based at state offices. I did not confirm whether the window is open in Oct 2026 or whether a recurring duty follows. The drive is mostly one-off, state-run and has low-income buyers who lack importer papers. Weak recurrence and willingness to pay. Market: 200,000 bikes registered in 3 months, plus 35,000 pending; no register total found.

The 2022 road code law is real and mandates driving-school training. But the implementing regulations (600+ articles) were not confirmed adopted as of Oct 2026. The latest source (March 2026) only says the minister is targeting H1 2026 and that the technical work is 80% done. I found no decree, no agrement or student-register reporting duty, and no count of schools. Competitor search found no Senegalese driving-school software, but results were mostly French or other-country pages. The only market figure is a vendor blog claiming about 90,000 permits a year (not official). Recurring reporting duty unproven, so the score stays low.

The framework convention is real (June 2026, SEN-CSU and ASPS). It covers clinics, practices, labs, imaging centres and pharmacies. It sets no billing mechanics. Specific per-provider conventions are still to come, so the recurring duty and its penalty are not yet defined. SEN-CSU already runs its own digital stack (SITFAC for billing follow-up, GESTAM, a national platform), so a state tool probably handles the core claims job. Kolonell and other Dakar vendors already sell IPM tiers-payant billing in clinic software, though those pages are marketing and their figures are unsourced. No register count was found, but private providers deliver about 45% of care. Pain is real, but the duty is vague, the state is likely to own the platform, and competitors exist. Not searched: Senegalese IPM claim rules and any SITFAC provider access.

Duty is real: DGES communiqué of 29 July 2026 restates law 94-82 and decree 2018-850. Opening, extension or relocation needs a full dossier, operation needs a provisional agrément, and breach can mean immediate closure. Reported figures are about 298 EPES, with roughly a third non-compliant (one source says about 100). Filing windows are one-off or yearly (2 Jan-31 Mar for opening; 2 Sep-2 Oct 2026 for 2027 LMD habilitation, online) and come from secondary sources. No competing software or state tool found, but only two searches were run. Weak case: the market is small (a few hundred buyers), filings are episodic, not a recurring monthly workflow, and the work is mostly consulting and paper dossiers. The 34-establishment and 333-total figures at lesoleil.sn were unreliable. Not checked: post-agrément annual reporting, and private primary or crèche duties.

Duty is real: Decree 2009-1226 requires a professional mareyeur card, with a category-3 exporter card issued per approved processing unit, prior declaration and an RCCM number (via search summary of faolex/DITP pages, not opened). Renewal cycle and penalties not found. No Senegalese software or DITP e-service found, but my search was shallow. Market size is not found: no register count, only the DITP approved list and the UPAMES association. The population is probably a few dozen to low hundreds of approved units, which is small. EU catch certificates are validated by DPM offices. Most exports go to Côte d'Ivoire and Mali (APS, Dec 2025). Low frequency, a small buyer pool and an informal sector make the case weak.
